name: Will Democrats win the U.S. Senate in 2026? (Democratic Party)
rule_notes: Kalshi settles early on a consensus of media calls, otherwise on the party of the Senate President pro tempore on Feb 1, 2027. Polymarket counts voting seats won, with independents counted for the party they caucus with. A 50-50 split goes to the party holding the Vice Presidency, and the first President pro tempore is the final fallback. Runoffs count, and it can stay open until Jan 4, 2027 if independent caucusing is unclear. Differences: Kalshi's summary does not spell out the 50-50 case, a post-election party switch counts on Kalshi but not Polymarket, and settlement timing can differ. Likely settles in November.

name: Will Democrats win the House in 2026? (Democratic Party)
rule_notes: Kalshi settles early on a consensus of media calls, otherwise on the party of the Speaker on Feb 1, 2027. Polymarket counts voting seats won, with independents counted for the party they caucus with. With no majority, it goes to the party of the first elected Speaker. Runoffs count, and it can stay open until Jan 4, 2027 if independent caucusing is unclear. Differences: a post-election party switch or a Speaker from the minority party counts on Kalshi but not Polymarket, and settlement timing can differ. Likely settles in November.

name: Will the Federal Reserve Hike rates by 25bps at their December 2026 meeting? (Hike 25bps)
rule_notes: Both resolve on the FOMC decision at the Dec 8-9, 2026 meeting, and the brackets match (a 50 bp hike is No for this market on both). Polymarket measures the change in the upper bound and rounds odd sizes up to the nearest 25 bp, so a 12.5 bp hike counts as 25. Kalshi's summary does not say how it treats odd sizes. If the meeting does not happen on its scheduled date, Kalshi resolves to maintains rate right away, while Polymarket waits until the next scheduled meeting before defaulting to no change, so a rescheduled meeting could split them.

name: Will Democratics win the Senate race in Texas? (James Talarico)
rule_notes: Kalshi pays Yes if a Democrat is sworn in as Texas senator for the term starting in 2027, with early settlement once a consensus of media organizations projects the winner. Polymarket resolves on the election winner, runoffs included, once AP, Fox News, and NBC all call it, otherwise on official certification. Independents never count as a party on Polymarket. Differences: Kalshi keys on who is sworn in and Polymarket on who wins, so a winner who is never seated would split them, and the media-call tests differ. Likely settles in early November. Date set to just after the January swearing-in.

name: Philadelphia wins (Philadelphia)
rule_notes: Both resolve on the official result of the Nov 1, 2026 Eagles vs Commanders game, overtime included, and a tie pays 50/50 on both. Difference: if the game is postponed and not started within 48 hours, Kalshi settles at a fair price, while Polymarket stays open until the game is played and only goes 50/50 if it is canceled with no makeup. Kickoff is 8:20 PM ET, so it settles after midnight UTC.

name: Buffalo wins (Buffalo)
rule_notes: Both resolve on the official result of the Nov 1, 2026 Ravens vs Bills game, overtime included, and a tie pays 50/50 on both. Difference: if the game is postponed and not started within 48 hours, Kalshi settles at a fair price, while Polymarket stays open until the game is played and only goes 50/50 if it is canceled with no makeup.

name: Will Los Angeles R win the 2027 Pro Football Championship? (Los Angeles R)
rule_notes: Both resolve Yes if the Rams win Super Bowl LXI on Feb 14, 2027. Polymarket resolves No as soon as the Rams are eliminated, and resolves to Other, which is No here, if the game is canceled or pushed past Mar 31, 2027. Kalshi's summary has no cancellation rule and its backstop close is Feb 2029, so a canceled or very late game could split them.

name: Will San Antonio win the 2027 Pro Basketball Finals? (San Antonio)
rule_notes: Both resolve Yes if the Spurs win the 2026-27 NBA title. Polymarket resolves No on elimination, breaks ties between multiple declared champions alphabetically, and resolves to Other, which is No here, if no champion is declared by Jun 30, 2027. Kalshi's summary has none of these rules and its backstop close is Jul 2029, so a canceled or delayed season could split them. Date set to the Polymarket deadline.

name: Will Colorado Avalanche win the 2026-27 Stanley Cup® Finals? (Colorado Avalanche)
rule_notes: Both resolve Yes if the Avalanche win the 2026-27 Stanley Cup. Polymarket resolves No on elimination, breaks ties between multiple declared champions alphabetically, and resolves to Other, which is No here, if no champion is declared by Jun 30, 2027. Kalshi's summary has none of these rules and its backstop close is Jun 2029, so a canceled or delayed season could split them. Date set to the Polymarket deadline.

name: Will Democratic win the Presidency in 2028? (Democratic party)
rule_notes: Kalshi pays Yes only if a Democrat is inaugurated for the term beginning Jan 20, 2029. Polymarket resolves once AP, Fox News, and NBC all call the race for the same party, falling back to who is inaugurated. Differences: Polymarket can settle on election-night calls in Nov 2028 while Kalshi waits for inauguration, and a called winner who is never inaugurated would split them. Date set to inauguration day.
